Forced side Titans: their close-loss pattern (5 of 7 games within 6, road losses all within 6) and the road tiebreaker. A healthy Ridley/Spears confirmation or Burrow-related news could have changed it; nothing decisive turned up.

Contaminated before any lean was written down, so it's locked as a pass. Before the leak I had only the line move toward Arizona (10.5 to 7) and SBR's short-week/overvalued-Dallas note, with no projection reached; the 7.0 projection is just the close. The forced side is the NFL road-side tiebreaker from LESSONS, applied mechanically ('no read'); it isn't a forecast.

I project Lions by about 2, which clears the slate's 3 by only 1 for Minnesota: a pass, made weaker because the slate's +3 is worse than the +3.5 close the previews liked. The best [angle] cuts against the Vikings: their record-setting blitz meets Goff, the league's best QB vs the blitz, and Minnesota's offense is 29th in EPA. Forced side Vikings: top defense vs Detroit's 31st-ranked one, plus the road tiebreaker. A confirmed St. Brown absence would have strengthened it; a full-go St. Brown with Jones out would have moved me toward a Lions pass.

This is a coin flip at 1.5 with no line movement. Both defenses are collapsing and both offenses can pass, so I project Jets by about 1. Most surprising [angle]: Geno Smith gets revenge on his old team while his head coach sits at 5-19. That's balanced by the Raiders' four-game defensive collapse. Forced side Raiders only as the NFL road tiebreaker for a game on the number ('no read' otherwise). A WagerTalk search snippet listed 'Raiders cover +1.5 / Over 45.5', which matched its own 27-24 Raiders prediction (a pick, not a result), so I didn't treat it as a leak, and the game was a pass regardless.

I project Steelers by about 3, a hook short of 3.5 in a low-total division game. That's inside the pass band: Cleveland's luck in one-score wins and Pittsburgh's 3-0 home ATS are both priced. Most surprising [angle]: the oldest Steelers team, home from Paris, with a bye next week. Forced side Browns: the line moved two points their way, the projection lands just under the hook, and the road tiebreaker applies. Clear news on Watson's protection (Tytus Howard's status) could have changed it.

I project Tampa by about 1.5 against a 2.5 line, a gap of 1. That is within the pass band, and the line already moved 2 points toward Atlanta. The surprising [angle] is Tampa's 0-4 home record with a QB who threw 11 passes in his return, but it's a narrative and the market has partly moved on it. The forced side is Atlanta, as the road dog the move went toward. Confirmation that Mayfield was limited, or a sharper late move, would have made it a pick.

The market moved 6 points to the close of -10.5 after the Nelson and Buckner trades and on Jacksonville's rest. I treat -10.5 as fair, which leaves the slate's -7.5 3 points better on Jacksonville. That is under the 4-point bar, and LESSONS says a stale slate number is information, not an edge (4-3). The surprising [angle] is a contender-level fire sale in game week. Confirmation that Warren and Gardner were out, or a projection past -11.5, would have made it a pick.

After a 3-point move I treat -6.5 as fair. I project the Rams by about 6, essentially on the number, so it's a pass. The bye-week line fixes (Alt and McConkey back) and the Rams' recent losses of Adams and Ford are the [angle], and they make the road side the tiebreaker per the NFL lesson. Evidence that the Chargers' line problems persisted, or a move back toward -5, would have changed the forced side.

This is a near pick'em at a stable number, and the evidence is balanced: Kansas City's run game and Denver's run-defense weakness against Kansas City's injured passing game and Denver's pass rush. I project Kansas City by about 1.5, on the number, so it's a pass. The forced side is the road team per the NFL tiebreaker lesson. Confirmation that Rice and Moore were out would have flipped the forced side to Denver.

The market held at 7 all week even after A.J. Brown and Henderson were ruled out. I project New England by about 7, so the slate's +7.5 is only half a point better on Miami and well inside the pass band. Getting the hook past 7 makes Miami the forced side, rather than the usual road tiebreaker. A close moving to -8 or more on New England would have flipped it.

The 8-point move on the Hurts news makes -5.5 the fair number. I project Washington by about 5, on the number, so it's a pass. The surprising [angle] is that Washington is itself depleted: Daniels winless in eight, McLaurin gone, and three DL starters hurt, which keeps the Eagles live despite McKee. That makes the road side the tiebreaker. Clear sharp money on Washington after the close, or the Washington DL being active, would have flipped it.

The Cross injury, Chicago's rest edge and its pass rush against a turnover-prone Darnold are real, but they came before the move from -4.5 to -3, so the close already prices them. Smith-Njigba against a weak Bears pass defense and Seattle's run defense against Chicago's run-heavy offense pull the other way. My projection (SEA by about 2.5) sits on the number, so I pass. The forced side goes to Chicago on the NFL road-team tiebreaker, plus the rest edge. A pick would have needed news after the line settled, such as Williams or Monangai being limited.
